/about.title: About | Cosmic Explorer
/about.description: About Cosmic Explorer - what it is, why it was built, its data sources, technology and team. A CSCI 3230U Web Development group project.

/asteroids.title: Near-Earth Asteroids | Cosmic Explorer
/asteroids.description: Search and filter the asteroids passing close to Earth in the coming weeks, using NASA's Near Earth Object Web Service.

/objects/betelgeuse.title: Betelgeuse | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/betelgeuse.description: A red supergiant on the edge of stellar death, so vast it would swallow the orbit of Jupiter if placed at our Sun.

/objects/crab-nebula.title: Crab Nebula | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/crab-nebula.description: The shredded remains of a supernova that Chinese astronomers recorded in 1054, now powered by a spinning neutron star.

/objects/earth.title: Earth | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/earth.description: The only world known to harbour life, with liquid water oceans covering 71 percent of its surface and a magnetic field that shields it.

/objects/europa.title: Europa | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/europa.description: An icy Jovian moon hiding a global saltwater ocean beneath its shell — a leading candidate for life beyond Earth.

/explore.title: Explore the Cosmos | Cosmic Explorer
/explore.description: Browse planets, moons, stars, galaxies and nebulae with Cosmic Explorer.

/objects/galaxy.title: Andromeda Galaxy | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/galaxy.description: Explore the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) - our nearest large galactic neighbor. Learn about its structure, collision course with the Milky Way, and stellar populations.

/objects/ganymede.title: Ganymede | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/ganymede.description: The largest moon in the solar system — bigger than the planet Mercury — and the only moon with its own magnetic field.

/objects/io.title: Io | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/io.description: The most volcanically active world in the solar system, kept molten by the tidal grip of Jupiter and its sibling moons.

/objects/jupiter.title: Jupiter | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/jupiter.description: Explore Jupiter - the largest planet in our solar system. Learn about its storms, moons, rings, and role as a cosmic shield.

/objects/mars.title: Mars | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/mars.description: Explore Mars - the Red Planet. Learn about its geography, atmosphere, exploration history, and potential for human settlement.

/objects/mercury.title: Mercury | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/mercury.description: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, a cratered world of rock with no atmosphere to soften its swings from scorching to freezing.

/milestones.title: Milestones | Cosmic Explorer
/milestones.description: The five project milestones for Cosmic Explorer, from team and topic to a deployed React application and demo video.

/objects/milky-way.title: Milky Way Galaxy | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/milky-way.description: Our home galaxy: a barred spiral of 100 to 400 billion stars, with a supermassive black hole at its centre.

/objects/moon.title: The Moon | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/moon.description: Earth's only natural satellite. Learn about its formation, phases, exploration history, and effects on Earth.

/objects/neptune.title: Neptune | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/neptune.description: The farthest planet from the Sun, a deep-blue ice giant driven by the fastest winds measured on any planet.

/objects/orion-nebula.title: Orion Nebula | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/orion-nebula.description: A stellar nursery 1,344 light-years away, and the brightest region of star formation visible to the naked eye.

/objects/proxima-centauri.title: Proxima Centauri | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/proxima-centauri.description: The closest star to the Sun, a cool red dwarf with at least one Earth-sized planet in its habitable zone.

/objects/rigel.title: Rigel | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/rigel.description: A blue supergiant marking the foot of Orion, shining roughly 120,000 times brighter than the Sun.

/objects/saturn.title: Saturn | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/saturn.description: Explore Saturn - the ringed planet. Learn about its spectacular rings, moons (including Titan and Enceladus), and unique features.

/objects/sirius.title: Sirius | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/sirius.description: The brightest star in Earth's night sky, a blue-white star twice the Sun's mass with a faint white dwarf companion.

/objects/sun.title: The Sun | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/sun.description: Explore the Sun - our star. Learn about its structure, energy production, solar activity, and importance to life on Earth.

/objects/titan.title: Titan | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/titan.description: Saturn's largest moon and the only moon with a thick atmosphere, where rivers and lakes are filled with liquid methane.

/objects/triangulum.title: Triangulum Galaxy | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/triangulum.description: The third-largest galaxy in our Local Group and the most distant object visible to the naked eye, 2.7 million light-years away.

/objects/triton.title: Triton | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/triton.description: Neptune's largest moon orbits backwards, and its frozen surface erupts geysers of nitrogen — a captured Kuiper Belt world.

/objects/uranus.title: Uranus | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/uranus.description: An ice giant tipped onto its side, rolling around the Sun with a 98-degree tilt that gives it seasons lasting 21 years each.

/objects/vega.title: Vega | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/vega.description: The fifth-brightest star in the sky and a calibration standard for astronomers, 25 light-years away in Lyra.

/objects/venus.title: Venus | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/venus.description: Earth's near-twin in size, wrapped in a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat until its surface glows at 464°C.

/objects/whirlpool.title: Whirlpool Galaxy | Cosmic Explorer
/objects/whirlpool.description: A grand-design spiral 31 million light-years away, caught mid-interaction with a smaller companion galaxy.
